title: [recoverability] Every restore drill (full, --only missions, --only transcripts, the controllers drill's sources) judges each unpacked bundle's tree before it reads anything of it, and reads a bundle's manifest only through a no-symlink, non-blocking, regular-file open: a symlinked manifest, transcript slice or repository bundle is refused without its target being opened (cc-astra A84)
prompt:
Spawn, objective 203 [recoverability], after 200 (cc-astra A84 HIGH, sync/astra/findings.md, 2026-11-15 16:34; the lead's contract of 2026-11-15; R1 author rev-g, reviewed by rev-f: FIX, the other drill modes; R2 author rev-f at the lead's word of 2026-11-16, reviewer rev-e): every restore drill judges each unpacked bundle's tree before it reads anything of it, and a bundle's manifest is never read through a symlink.

Base: live main 6f8ceb8c (R1 was written on 560e2980; main has touched no file of 203 since).

The problem. `spawn backup restore-drill --only transcripts` (objective 200) promises that a symlink in a bundle is never followed. But fetch_members ends in read_manifest, and read_manifest reads unpacked/manifest.json with fs::read, which follows a symlink. Only after fetch_members returns does the drill run plain_tree on the unpacked tree. So a bundle whose recorded sha256 matches (no mismatch, no race, no credential needed), holding a manifest.json that is a symlink to a readable file outside the drill folder, gets that file opened and read before the refusal. The same fs::read serves every drill (full, missions, controllers).

Read first: crates/spawn-cli/src/backup/restore_drill.rs (run's Only::Transcripts arm, fetch_members, read_manifest, plain_tree, fetch_bundle; the controllers drill's fetch_members call).

What changes (spawn-cli, restore_drill.rs only):
- read_plain_file(path) (new). It opens with rustix O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK | O_CLOEXEC, checks with fstat on the open file that it is a regular file, and only then reads it.
  - A symlink reads "a symlink, never followed" (ELOOP); a missing file, "not in the bundle".
  - A FIFO, device or directory reads "not a regular file, never read", and is never waited on.
- read_manifest reads manifest.json through read_plain_file, for every drill. Its errors read "<key>'s manifest.json: <why>".
- unpacked_manifest(key, record, unpacked) (new): plain_tree(unpacked) first, then read_manifest. Every drill reaches the unpacked tree through it, so nothing of a bundle is read before its tree holds only directories and regular files:
  - fetch_members ends in it (--only transcripts, --only missions, and the controllers drill's sources); the transcripts arm no longer calls plain_tree after fetch_members, since it now runs inside, before the manifest;
  - fetch_bundle (the full drill, no --only) ends in it too.
  - Why every mode (R2): the full drill unpacks the whole bundle, then restore_transcripts opens each slice the manifest names with File::open, which follows a symlink; --only missions hands repos/<file> (the record's) to git clone --mirror, which follows one too. Real bundles hold no symlink, FIFO or device: the bundle unit writes the manifest (fs::write), each transcript slice (append_slice) and each repository bundle (fs::copy) as new regular files in its staging folder, then tars that folder. So no real drill is refused by it.
- Nothing else changes: the listing, the members chosen, the two streams and their sha256 checks, restore and judge, the final plain_tree of the drill folder, the record, and the folder's removal rules (a plain-only folder holding a symlink is left, said).

Tests (spawn-cli backup::restore_drill):
- a_symlinked_manifest_is_refused_before_its_target_is_opened (new, Linux). unpacked/manifest.json is a symlink to a FIFO in a sibling folder, and a witness thread waits to open that FIFO for writing. An open for reading would let the witness through, so "not opened" is observed, not inferred.
  - Read two ways, through unpacked_manifest (every drill's path, the tree judged first) and through read_manifest alone (the no-follow read): refused, naming a symlink, and the witness still waits.
  - Then manifest.json as a FIFO itself: refused with no wait, as "neither a directory nor a regular file" by the tree's judgement and as "not a regular file" by the manifest read alone.
  - A regular manifest of the record's kind: read both ways.
  - Then a repository bundle beside it that is a symlink (R2): unpacked_manifest refuses it, naming x.bundle as a symlink.
- No test is renamed or dropped; the existing restore_drill tests pass.

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/backup/restore_drill.rs. The owner's part: rsi/scenarios/203.sh (new), rsi/backlog/203.json.
Size: restore_drill.rs about +55 -12 in code, plus a test of about 100 lines (R2: -47 +56 over R1, the `plain` flag gone); 203.sh about 980 lines (200.sh's harness up to its step (1), then 6 checks; R2 +115).

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/203.sh, black box, on its own database, scratch HOME and GNUPGHOME, against 104's local R2 stand-in (200.sh's harness).
- (1) The bundle unit records backup.bundled (setup).
- (2) The newest bundle's object is replaced by a crafted tar, encrypted under the same passphrase. Its ./manifest.json is a symlink to a FIFO outside the drill folder, beside one regular slice. The record's sha256 and the object's x-amz-meta-sha256 are set to the crafted stream's, so only the tree's types can refuse it. A witness waits to open the FIFO for writing and leaves a marker once anything opens it for reading. The drill (--only transcripts) must:
  - exit 1 within 120 s;
  - record backup.drilled.transcripts ok false, its reason naming manifest.json as a symlink;
  - leave no marker, with the witness still waiting and the FIFO still there.
- (3) The same with a regular manifest of the record's kind naming two transcript slices, one of which (y.jsonl) is the symlink to the FIFO: exit 1, the reason names y.jsonl as a symlink, and the FIFO is never opened.
- (4) R2: the full drill (no --only) over (3)'s bundle: exit 1 within 120 s, backup.drilled.transcripts ok false naming y.jsonl as a symlink, and the FIFO never opened (the full drill restores the transcripts first).
- (5) R2: --only missions over a bundle whose repository bundle (the file the record names first under repos/) is a symlink to the FIFO, beside a regular manifest of the record's kind: exit 1, backup.drilled.missions ok false naming that file as a symlink, and git never opens the FIFO.
- (6) R2: (2)'s bundle under --only missions and under the full drill: each exits 1, backup.drilled.missions ok false naming manifest.json as a symlink, and the FIFO never opened.
Which check holds each guard:
- the tree judged in unpacked_manifest (fetch_members's drills): 203.sh (3) and (5);
- the tree judged in fetch_bundle (the full drill): 203.sh (4) and (6)'s full-drill run;
- the no-follow, non-blocking, regular-only manifest read: the unit test alone. Every drill judges the tree first, so no bundle reaches the manifest read with a symlink, a FIFO or a device in it. It is the second guard, kept and tested, not reachable black-box.
On the base (6f8ceb8c, 200 as landed) 203.sh exits 1 at (2): "the FIFO outside the drill folder was opened through the bundle's manifest.json symlink (the witness got through)". R1 (a2192ac3) passes (2) and (3) and exits 1 at (4): the full drill opens the slice.

Verified by: the gate runs 203.sh. Live, the daily transcripts drill (06:15) keeps passing on real bundles, which hold no symlink: its record stays ok true with "<n> of <n> files as the newest record's sha256".
